text:
maria: Heads up — saw a 95th/99th tail spike on the kvcache prefetch path on prod-gpu-3 during the midday load test. Captured an nsys timeline. Looks like H2D memcpy on stream 2 is delaying a small compute kernel on stream 1 for ~4–6ms intermittently. :thinking:

alex: Can you paste the nsys capture command / perf flags you used? Also which branch/commit was running?

maria: Ran: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --output=/tmp/trace` against commit e4f8a3c (batcher heuristics change). Capture snippet:

```
# timeline notes
Host thread TID 4123: prefetch worker (kvcache)
CUDA stream 2: cudaMemcpy H2D pinnedBuf -> device (0.25ms)
CUDA stream 1: small int8 kernel (0.8ms) waiting on stream 2 completion ~4.2ms later
CPU sleep/wakeup gap ~3.5ms observed between host memcpy and ioctl/kick
```

kevin: Hmm. Two quick hypotheses: (1) memcpy is pageable -> synchronous stall, or (2) CPU scheduling preemption on prefetch thread so kernel enqueue is delayed. Which allocator did you use for the host buffer?

maria: Using our kvcache default which currently uses registered pages via cudaHostRegister but fallbacks to malloc if registration fails. This node had occasional registration faults (we log them).

tara: If registration failed it could be falling back to pageable memcpy which blocks on the CPU and causes a wakeup delay on the worker thread. That would serialize GPU work. Also check if the prefetch thread is pinned to the same CPU core as the main worker — contention + CFS slice could amplify the delay.

alex: I noticed the batcher heuristic change moved prefetch to be eager for sequences > 128 tokens. That increases prefetch frequency and CPU work. If the prefetch worker is single-threaded that could create jitter.

maria: Good catch — e4f8a3c is exactly the change that ramps prefetch concurrency down to 1 for memory safety. We rolled it out to a few hosts. Rollback test to ef3b21 (old heuristic) reduced 99th by ~12% in our synthetic test earlier today.

kevin: Can you share a short stack/trace for the host thread around the memcpy? nvprof or perf sample would help. If we see `__page_fault` or `copy_user_enhanced_fast_string` it means host pages are being faulted in. If it's `epoll_wait`/`nanosleep` then scheduling.

maria: Pasted a perf sample from the same window: `copy_user_enhanced_fast_string` shows up ~0.18% but we have `__do_page_fault` hits on rare samples. Most weight is `poll`/`futex` indicating wakeup latency.

tara: Actionable: (A) ensure prefetch uses pinned buffers (cudaHostAlloc/REGISTER) and fail early if registration fails, (B) move prefetch onto isolated cpuset or increase thread priority for the worker, (C) sample with perf + nvprof for 60s and share the .qdrep.

maria: I'll schedule a short canary: toggle eager prefetch off and force pinned allocation with retries, then run `nsys profile --capture-range split --capture-range-start cudaMemcpy --capture-range-end kernel` for 30s during load.

perf-bot: Note: created perf job #3421 capturing 30s nsys on prod-gpu-3 at 16:00 UTC.

alex: Also check kernel selection: small int8 kernels sometimes branch to a different kernel with additional synchronization if sequence length > threshold. If memcpy latency pushes enqueue past the window, scheduler picks slower kernel variant. Can you grep for `kernel_select()` NVTX markers?

maria: I do have NVTX markers in the runtime. In the capture I see `kernel_select:fast_int8` then later `kernel_select:safe_int8` around delayed cases. Might be our heuristic fallback when prefetched KV not ready.

kevin: That explains higher tail. Two parallel fixes: reduce fallback aggressiveness + mask small delays (tolerate short prefetch latency before fallback). Also consider a tiny async callback that enqueues kernels once memcpy completes instead of relying on host ordering.

tara: If we implement an enqueue-on-completion path we must ensure we don't blow up device queue depth. Add an upper bound to outstanding async enqueues.

maria: Agreed. Immediate plan: revert the eager prefetch change in the canary, force pinned host allocation, and collect another nsys + perfetto trace. If tail improves we have a smoking gun. I'll upload the .qdrep and a 10s perfetto UI link here after capture. :eyes:

alex: Thanks — ping us when the trace is uploaded. If it's positive, we should roll a targeted fix: make prefetch allocation strict (fail fast) + bump prefetch thread priority and instrument NVTX around kernel_select to correlate.

maria: Will do. TL;DR for the channel: intermittent 4–6ms enqueue delays from prefetch path on commit e4f8a3c likely due to fallback pageable memcpy + CPU scheduling gaps causing kernel fallback to slower variant. Repro plan and immediate mitigations listed above.

kevin: One more micro tip — add a small host-side busy-spin of ~100us after memcpy completion to keep the prefetch thread scheduled long enough to enqueue, sometimes reduces wake jitter without cpuset surgery (use carefully).

maria: noted. I'll test both priority and the tiny spin. Thanks all.
